title: Universo de Leyes
description:
Universo de Leyes turns Mexican legal documents into a navigable citation network. I built the annotated dataset and information-extraction pipeline used to identify legal entities and references, then fine-tuned a RoBERTa model and trained a spaCy NER pipeline to structure those relationships.

The interface presents laws and their citations as a knowledge graph, helping researchers trace how one text depends on another instead of searching documents one at a time. The work led to a peer-reviewed paper presented at ICITS 2025. Current research uses text and graph embeddings to study how Mexican law changes over time.
publications: Valdés, F., Gomar, R. H., & Méndez, D. A. (2025). Comparative Analysis of Information Extraction Techniques in the Mexican Legal System. In Information Technology and Systems, ICITS 2025, Volume 3, Conference proceedings, Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems.

title: Ethics Survey Answer Clustering
description: This project aims to quantify and analyze differences in survey answers from over 200 ethics class tutors in Mexico City. The tutors each answered a survey of 10 open-ended questions. To aid investigators in finding correlations between tutor responses and the subsequent performance of their students, this project seeks to develop an automated method for grouping and clustering the textual answers, uncovering underlying patterns and themes.

title: Futbol Transformer
description: A personal project undertaken with the pedagogical goal of deeply exploring the transformer architecture. The core idea is to treat football (soccer) players and their on-field actions as words and sentences. By applying NLP techniques, I aim to predict which player will make the next move in a sequence and, hopefully, discover real-world tactical knowledge embedded within the model's results. This project is currently in progress.

title: COSMIC NLP Automation
description:
During two internships at Spingere, I was tasked with creating a prototype of an NLP system to automatically extract COSMIC software functional size estimation points from written project requirement documents. My role involved the complete research, planning, and prototyping of the solution. I organized and coordinated meetings with leading NLP specialists in Mexico to facilitate knowledge exchange.

The technical approach involved extracting actionable subject-verb-object triplets from the documents and training a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model to categorize the verbs based on real COSMIC data. The initial exploration yielded an F-score of 60% compared to expert human analysis, which was deemed promising enough for the company to pursue further internal development.

title: ANTAD Pharmacy Site Recommendation
description:
This project was developed for the 2024 ITAM Datathon, where it secured a finalist position among the top 6 teams out of 54. The objective was to use machine learning models, trained on data from high-performing pharmacies, to identify strategic locations for new store openings. This involved a comparative analysis of regional economic indicators to inform the site selection process. By analyzing open data from INEGI and considering key economic and demographic variables, we strategically selected municipalities for expansion.

Key Results:
- Model Performance: The prediction model, trained on 1,375 data points with 45 input variables, achieved an R² Score of 0.9677 and an RMSE of 23.2862, optimized using XGBoost.
- Market Analysis: Analyzed 1,156 municipalities, identifying 441 as high-potential.
- Strategic Recommendation: Recommended 46 municipalities across 20 states for new pharmacy openings, representing a potential market value of 1.33 billion pesos.

title: Gol Tempranero
description:
Developed for the Hackathon Football Analytics ITAM 2024, this project earned a finalist spot among the top 5 teams out of 120. The project investigated whether early goals in football matches are a result of specific, repeatable strategies or merely luck. By analyzing 333 matches with early goals across competitions like the Bundesliga, Champions League, and Copa América, we found that the scoring team achieved a win or draw in 69.3% of cases.

Using StatsBomb event data, we generated and classified play sequences leading to early goals, analyzing variables like pass height, length, and type. The K-Means algorithm was applied to identify recurring tactical patterns, revealing that different leagues and teams employ distinct strategies to score early. The analysis concluded that while early goals significantly impact results, they necessitate specific strategic planning.

title: SEMOVI Route Reconstruction Pipeline
description:
SEMOVI held public-transport route records as scanned documents and written street-by-street directions. I built a pipeline that converts those records into geospatial routes.

The system cleans each scan, extracts the route description with OCR, resolves street names against OpenStreetMap, and reconstructs the path on a digital map. It reduces the manual work required to turn archival route records into data that planners can inspect and analyze. I am documenting the extraction and route-building methods in a research paper.

title: Auto-parts catalogue extraction and matching
description:
I collaborated with InvierteSustentable and JetzApp on a prototype for comparing automotive parts across supplier catalogues with different schemas, labels and document formats. The work combined catalogue extraction, a shared categorization scheme and matching of compatible alternatives. The broader system tracks parts and repair options for more than 300 vehicle models.

The catalogue extraction experiment was part of this project. An Observer–Analyzer–Coder agent system generated and revised Python Pandas code to clean and standardize catalogues digitized with Camelot and OCR. It correctly formatted 4 of 10 brand catalogues without human intervention. Inconsistent manufacturer layouts remained a limitation, and this experiment was put on hold.
presentations: Presented at the Centro ITAM para Datos + Algoritmos + Sociedad annual project presentation in 2024 and 2025.

title: Tellus: Geospatial ATM Expansion Planning
description:
Tellus is a geospatial planning system for comparing prospective ATM locations. As the full-stack ML engineer, I built the spatial database, data pipeline, backend API, prediction models, and map-based interface used to review recommendations.

The database combines more than 12,000 ATMs with monthly transaction data from four banks. A municipality-level model estimates ATM demand with an R² of 0.92, while a second model estimates monthly transactions at a candidate site with an R² of 0.60. The system identified 30 high-potential BanCoppel locations whose rankings closely matched recommendations from the bank's location experts.

title: Retail Informality Prioritization Model
description:
For INEGI Datatón 2025, our team built a policy-prioritization model to identify where interventions could have the greatest effect on commercial informality in Mexico. The analysis won the competition.

We combined Economic Census data with wages, social-security coverage, educational attainment, product category, and regional indicators. Instead of producing a single national ranking, the model distinguishes the barriers facing different products, places, and business segments, then connects each pattern to a more targeted policy response.

title: Teaching at MIT IAP and MIT Sloan
description: I served as an instructor and lecturer for MIT IAP courses 6.S189 and 6.S187 and MIT Sloan 15.S65. Teaching covered applied AI, machine learning and deployment.

title: El Critón Interactivo
description: I created a comprehensive and interactive digital interpretation of Plato’s dialogue "Crito" to serve as an engaging educational resource for first-semester students in the "Ideas e Instituciones Políticas I" course at ITAM. A narrative closely based on the source text was designed, applying game design principles to enhance content interaction and information recall. A use-case-specific dialogue system was built from the ground up using Angular.

title: Space Train
description: A personal website that serves as my professional portfolio and a creative outlet. Conceived more as a continuous journey than a final product, this project has been instrumental in helping me learn and refine a variety of web development and design skills.

title: CASAPP
description: My first significant software development project. I built a robust Angular website for my high school classmates to keep track of their CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service) activities for the IB program. The application featured user authentication, image uploading, and a complete activity management system, all built on a Firebase backend.

title: Datodos
description: A website launched during the COVID-19 pandemic to facilitate the donation of cellular data to underprivileged students who lacked home internet access for their online classes. The initiative successfully raised 2,000 pesos, providing five students with enough internet access to attend their classes for three months.

title: AuthentiQR
description: An Android application built for the ITAM 2023 Hackathon. In the post-COVID era of QR-code menus, this app provides a layer of security by allowing a user to scan a QR code and check its destination link against various security APIs and databases to ensure it is not malicious. The project won first place in the competition.

title: Latent Lull
description: My passion project: a video game currently in development.

title: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe AI
description: A project for my 5th-semester Artificial Intelligence class. I built an Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe game engine and an AI opponent. The AI's board evaluation function is powered by a neural network, which feeds into a foundational Minimax algorithm with alpha-beta pruning. I personally cannot beat it.

title: La Baldosa de Hisarlik
description: A Unity-based interactive experience inspired by an animation I created in OpenGL. The project is based on a specific story from Homer's Iliad—the Trojan Horse—but with the narrative constraint of telling the story through the visuals found on a single, unearthed archaeological tile.

title: Mara Triangle Safari Route Simulation
description: A rule-based agent simulation of 15 different animal species found in the Mara Triangle. The simulation was constructed to test what effect safari vehicles following designated routes have on the animal population's behavior and distribution.

title: Sense It
description: For my Principles of Mechatronics class, I built a "Bop It" style game from scratch. The project involved writing 2,500 lines of AVR assembly code to control the game logic. It incorporated three analogue sensors and two digital sensors, an Arduino as an analogue-to-digital converter, and utilized AVR timers, delays, and PWM for audio-visual feedback. A 7-segment digital display system shows the score. The game randomly selects a sensor, and the player must interact with it in time, with the time limit decreasing as the game progresses. The toy was designed and constructed from 3d laser cut parts designed using SolidWorks.

title: Basic CPU from Logic Gates
description: Using the Quartus design software, I built a functional CPU from basic logic gates. The system is capable of performing 8-bit addition, subtraction, and multiplication. The design included a datapath, memory path, program counter, and an arithmetic logic unit (ALU). The final CPU was connected to a breadboard with analogue inputs and a 4-digit, 7-segment display for output.

title: 3D Scanning Course
description: For two semesters, I served as the lead 3D scanner in the maker lab's design team. In this role, I taught a class of 12 students how to effectively use the CR Lizard 3D scanner to scan functional parts and subsequently replicate or modify them using SolidWorks.

title: Hierarchical topic modeling and Tree Atlas
description:
I am developing methods for organizing document collections into readable topic hierarchies. The work separates document grouping, the construction of parent and child relationships, and the language used to describe each group. I compare embedding and lexical representations, generated topic labels, and bounded repairs on banking questions, DBpedia texts and Mexican legal documents.

I built Tree Atlas to inspect the resulting trees alongside their documents, original-space neighbors, source evidence and recorded evaluation results. It makes it possible to compare methods and examine where an apparently coherent branch breaks down.

This is ongoing research. Some changes improve fine-grained grouping while damaging broader structure; a clear-looking map does not establish a correct taxonomy. The experiments retain these failures alongside the useful local examples.

title: MAKERS platform
description:
I am consolidating MAKERS' public website, order handling and internal lab tools into a shared platform. The ethos is to kill a mosquito with a bazooka: use a university makerspace to work through the architecture of a much larger system.

The pnpm and Turborepo monorepo contains three Next.js applications, Site, Pedidos and Gestión, backed by a Django API and PostgreSQL. My work includes shared interface components, generated API contracts, a common identity model, and permissions for lab operations. A person can place an order without being a Maker; Maker membership carries its own hours, training and equipment permissions.

The platform also includes order and production workflows, private uploads, and website administration with drafts, publication review, image management and revision history. I worked on migration tools and rehearsals to reconcile the older systems while keeping them available. The new platform is being migrated alongside the existing applications.

title: Mapa ITAM and the academic atlas
description:
Working with the MAKERS team, I contributed to ITAM's interactive campus map and developed an academic-atlas extension for exploring the university's research. The physical map supports room search and campus navigation. The atlas connects public faculty profiles, publications, research topics and recorded coauthorship.

My work includes gathering and organizing source records, building topic representations, and designing linked views for people, departments, semantic neighborhoods and collaborations. Each view leads back to the text and publications behind a connection.

The visual forms answer different questions: a department-topic matrix gives an overview, semantic projections support exploration, and a focused coauthor network keeps individual relationships readable. Textual similarity is presented as affinity rather than a ranking of researchers. The atlas is also part of the broader MAKERS platform work.
contribution: Collaborative map development, data and atlas design

title: Espacios Latentes
description:
Through MAKERS, I collaborated on organizing Espacios Latentes, an AI gathering at ITAM on 23 and 24 October 2026. The encounter combines talks, discussion and hands-on work.

Alongside that organizing work, I helped build the bilingual website and the tools supporting the event: registration, attendee questionnaires, organizer views and campus wayfinding.

title: Mexican parliamentary discourse
description:
I mentored this MAKERS project on the computational analysis of Mexican parliamentary debates. The work includes a collection and structuring pipeline, analysis scripts and a dashboard for exploring language across legislatures and parties. The pipeline downloads session records, extracts interventions and organizes speakers and party affiliations.

The analysis explores evidence-oriented and intuition-oriented language using Word2Vec representations, alongside lexical and procedural indicators. The dashboard brings these views together with access to their methods. These are exploratory measures of discourse; they do not establish the quality of an argument or verify whether its claims are true.

title: Artist references in music criticism
description:
I mentored this MAKERS project exploring how Pitchfork reviewers use other artists as reference points. The project brings together album reviews, artist metadata and artist mentions to study comparisons in the language of music criticism.

The notebooks cover data cleaning, artist-name matching and the construction of directed reference networks. The narrower analysis separates comparison, influence language and broader references, retaining the review sentences behind each relationship.

This is collaborative, exploratory research. A reference in a review describes a critic's framing; it does not by itself establish historical musical influence.
